title: Thousands of Fancy Dishes Have Survived a 2,100-Year-Old Shipwreck - Nautilus
gist: An Akdeniz University team in Türkiye has recovered 6,511 well-preserved ceramic plates, bowls and trays in 122 forms and sizes from a 2,100-year-old Mediterranean shipwreck near Adrasan; the pieces have been moved to the Antalya Museum.

insights.claim: A team from Akdeniz University in Türkiye has recovered the expensive ceramic cargo of a 2,100-year-old Mediterranean shipwreck, which survived far better than would be expected.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Exceptional preservation enhances the archaeological and cultural-tourism value of the find.
insights.quote: But that’s not the case with the expensive freight of a wrecked boat recovered by a team from Akdeniz University in Türkiye.

insights.claim: The recovered shipwreck haul totals 6,511 ceramic plates, bowls and trays in 122 different forms and sizes.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Volume and standardization of wares point to large-scale ancient Mediterranean trade in tableware.
insights.quote: To date, the haul includes 6,511 ceramic plates, bowls, and trays, in a total of 122 different forms and sizes.

insights.claim: The shipwreck ceramics, found near the village of Adrasan, have been transferred to the Antalya Museum about 55 miles away.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Adds a notable collection to a regional museum in a major Turkish tourism area.
